selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Reverts loop-memcpy hoisting in LoopIdiomRecognize. It removes the generic memory-intrinsic processing helper and the loop memcpy recognition path that promoted strided per-iteration memcpys into a larger preheader operation; loop-block processing is restored to scanning only memset intrinsics for this class of transformation.
Changed symbols: LoopIdiomRecognize::runOnLoopBlock; LoopIdiomRecognize::processLoopMemIntrinsic; LoopIdiomRecognize::processLoopMemCpy; LoopIdiomRecognize::processLoopStoreOfLoopLoad
Behavioral change: Stops invoking the loop memcpy processor from runOnLoopBlock.; Deletes recognition of non-volatile, constant-size loop memcpys with affine source and destination SCEVs and matching strides.; Prevents the removed memcpy path from calling processLoopStoreOfLoopLoad to form a promoted/hoisted memory operation.; Retains the explicit iterator-safe scan for loop memset processing.
Assertion or trace link: optimizer; dominance; preheader; Verifier
Reproducer link: The issue occurs under optimization, and this commit disables a loop optimization that hoisted memcpy-derived work to a loop preheader. No retrieved test or hunk demonstrates the PR50585 C testcase, its exact IR, or the reported dominance diagnostic.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopIdiomRecognize; llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopIdiomRecognize.cpp; LoopInfo; DominatorTree; ScalarEvolution
Causal explanation: The reverted transformation explicitly moved loop memcpy behavior to a preheader. Such motion is directly sensitive to whether source operands and derived values are available at the new location, making it materially relevant to an "Instruction does not dominate all uses" failure. This commit removes, rather than introduces, that hoisting path, so the visible evidence more strongly supports it as a potential mitigation/fix boundary for a dominance bug in the reverted feature than as an introducer. The connection remains indirect because no PR50585-specific reproducer or verifier test is present.
Causal confidence: 0.63

top_candidates.subject: [MemCpyOpt] Allow variable lengths in memcpy optimizer
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Extends MemCpyOpt to handle equal non-constant memcpy/memset lengths while preserving constant-size requirements for transformations that need numeric length comparisons. The change adjusts dependence, undef-content, and memcpy-to-memset reasoning so variable length Values can be propagated or compared by identity, while tail-reduction and lifetime-size checks remain restricted to constant lengths.
Changed symbols: MemCpyOptPass::processMemCpyMemCpyDependence; MemCpyOptPass::processMemCpy; hasUndefContents; hasUndefContentsMSSA; MemCpyOptPass::performMemCpyToMemSetOptzn
Behavioral change: Allows a memcpy-dependence optimization when the two memcpy length operands are the same Value, even when that Value is not a ConstantInt.; Uses the original memcpy length Value rather than CopySize when checking whether a source dependency has undef contents.; Permits variable memset lengths in memcpy-to-memset analysis, but requires a constant memcpy size where the optimization must compare sizes or reduce the copy range.; Restricts constant lifetime-start coverage comparisons to cases where the queried size is constant, while retaining the whole-alloca undef reasoning path.; For a constant memcpy larger than a constant memset, requires MemorySSA or memory-dependence evidence that the uncovered tail was undef before reducing the copy to the memset size.
Assertion or trace link: optimizer; LLVM scalar transformation
Reproducer link: The retrieved change concerns memcpy/memset length and undef-memory analysis; no compact C reproducer, dominance diagnostic, or verifier failure is shown.
Pass or subsystem link: MemCpyOpt; llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/MemCpyOptimizer.cpp; MemorySSA; AliasAnalysis
Causal explanation: This is an O1-relevant scalar optimizer change that broadens when memory-copy rewrites can occur, so an incorrect memory transformation could in principle participate in an optimizer failure. However, the visible hunks alter memory-size and undef-content legality checks rather than CFG construction, instruction motion, value replacement, or dominance maintenance. There is no direct evidence tying these rewrites to the reported "Instruction does not dominate all uses" verifier failure.
Causal confidence: 0.18
Build risk: The change modifies several interacting MemCpyOpt legality paths, including MemorySSA and non-MemorySSA handling.; No test hunk is retrieved for this commit.; Coverage reports 12 omitted hunks, so the visible patch does not establish complete test or integration coverage.

Summary: This commit changes LoopUnroll's handling of conditional branches during peeling and full unrolling. It removes the PreserveCondBr argument from the LoopUnrollPass call, derives an exact trip count for the exiting branch, and revises the decision logic for retaining or folding cloned conditional branches based on preserve-only-first, exact-unroll, maximum-trip-count, and exact-trip-count cases. The accompanying test updates show changed loop CFG and PHI structure after peeling/complete-unroll handling.
Changed symbols: llvm::UnrollLoop; UnrollLoopOptions; tryToUnrollLoop; PreserveCondBr; test1
Behavioral change: UnrollLoop computes ExactTripCount using ScalarEvolution for the exiting branch's parent block and derives ExactUnroll from whether that count equals the requested unroll count.; The old PreserveCondBr-based branch-preservation decision is removed.; For preserve-only-first unrolling, the decision now depends on the unrolled-copy index; for exact unrolling it preserves only the first conditional case; for full but non-exact unrolling it folds or retains branch outcomes using j, MaxTripCount, and ExactTripCount.; The calculation of CompletelyUnroll and RuntimeTripCount is moved to the later setup region identified by comments as occurring after peeling-sensitive values may have changed.; The regression test now expects altered PHI incoming values, additional peeled iterations, and an explicit constant conditional branch/exit structure.
Assertion or trace link: No literal 'Instruction does not dominate all uses' or verifier diagnostic appears in the retrieved hunks.; The changed code directly controls loop conditional branches, cloned iteration exits, and test-observed PHI/CFG shape, which are structures whose incorrect rewiring can produce dominance violations.

Summary: This change strengthens `Verifier::visitIntrinsicCall` validation for experimental vector insert/extract intrinsics. It obtains the vector operands and constant index, requires the index to be a multiple of the inserted or extracted vector's known minimum element count, and rejects fixed/fixed or scalable/scalable operations whose selected subvector range overruns the parent vector. New verifier tests cover invalid multiples and overruns, while mixed scalable-parent/fixed-subvector cases remain exempt from static overrun checking.

@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+; RUN: not opt -verify -S < %s 2>&1 >/dev/null | FileCheck %s
+
+;
+; Test that extractions/insertion indices are validated.
+;
+
+; CHECK: experimental_vector_extract index must be a constant multiple of the result type's known minimum vector length.
+define <4 x i32> @extract_idx_not_constant_multiple(<8 x i32> %vec) {
+  %1 = call <4 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.extract.v4i32.v8i32(<8 x i32> %vec, i64 1)
+  ret <4 x i32> %1
+}
+
+; CHECK: experimental_vector_insert index must be a constant multiple of the subvector's known minimum vector length.
+define <8 x i32> @insert_idx_not_constant_multiple(<8 x i32> %vec, <4 x i32> %subvec) {
+  %1 = call <8 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.insert.v8i32.v4i32(<8 x i32> %vec, <4 x i32> %subvec, i64 2)
+  ret <8 x i32> %1
+}
+
+;
+; Test that extractions/insertions which 'overrun' are captured.
+;
+
+; CHECK: experimental_vector_extract would overrun.
+define <3 x i32> @extract_overrun_fixed_fixed(<8 x i32> %vec) {
+  %1 = call <3 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.extract.v8i32.v3i32(<8 x i32> %vec, i64 6)
+  ret <3 x i32> %1
+}
+
+; CHECK: experimental_vector_extract would overrun.
+define <vscale x 3 x i32> @extract_overrun_scalable_scalable(<vscale x 8 x i32> %vec) {
+  %1 = call <vscale x 3 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.extract.nxv8i32.nxv3i32(<vscale x 8 x i32> %vec, i64 6)
+  ret <vscale x 3 x i32> %1
+}
+
+; We cannot statically check whether or not an extraction of a fixed vector
+; from a scalable vector would overrun, because we can't compare the sizes of
+; the two. Therefore, this function should not raise verifier errors.
+; CHECK-NOT: experimental_vector_extract
+define <3 x i32> @extract_overrun_scalable_fixed(<vscale x 8 x i32> %vec) {
+  %1 = call <3 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.extract.nxv8i32.v3i32(<vscale x 8 x i32> %vec, i64 6)
+  ret <3 x i32> %1
+}
+
+; CHECK: subvector operand of experimental_vector_insert would overrun the vector being inserted into.
+define <8 x i32> @insert_overrun_fixed_fixed(<8 x i32> %vec, <3 x i32> %subvec) {
+  %1 = call <8 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.insert.v8i32.v3i32(<8 x i32> %vec, <3 x i32> %subvec, i64 6)
+  ret <8 x i32> %1
+}
+

+define <vscale x 8 x i32> @insert_overrun_scalable_scalable(<vscale x 8 x i32> %vec, <vscale x 3 x i32> %subvec) {
+  %1 = call <vscale x 8 x i32> @llvm.experimental.vector.insert.nxv8i32.nxv3i32(<vscale x 8 x i32> %vec, <vscale x 3 x i32> %subvec, i64 6)
+  ret <vscale x 8 x i32> %1
+}
+
+; We cannot statically check whether or not an insertion of a fixed vector into
+; a scalable vector would overrun, because we can't compare the sizes of the

steps.subject: [SimplifyCFG] Fix SimplifyBranchOnICmpChain to be undef/poison safe.

evidence: Directly modifies SimplifyCFG, an O1-relevant scalar CFG-rewriting pass that creates blocks, rewrites branches, and changes value-use placement.
Although the stated fix is poison/undef semantics via freeze rather than a reported dominance repair, this is by far the closest concrete CFG/value-use transformation among the candidates.
features: cfg-rewrite, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/Utils, path:llvm/test/Transforms/SimplifyCFG, poison-freeze, simplifycfg
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This changes SimplifyCFG's branch-on-icmp-chain rewrite so that it is safe when the extra branch condition may be undef or poison. Rather than disabling the transformation for MemorySanitizer functions, the rewrite now freezes an ExtraCase value unless it is proven not undef/poison, preserving defined control-flow semantics while allowing the switch-creation transformation to run.
Changed symbols: SimplifyCFGOpt::SimplifyBranchOnICmpChain; test_msan; test_no_msan
Behavioral change: Removes the SanitizeMemory-specific early return that previously prevented the ExtraCase transformation.; Uses isGuaranteedNotToBeUndefOrPoison with the pass AssumptionCache to determine whether ExtraCase requires protection.; Inserts freeze on a potentially undef-or-poison ExtraCase before it is used as the rewritten branch condition.; Updates SimplifyCFG regression expectations so the transformed CFG branches on the frozen value and can route through switch.early.test.
Assertion or trace link: No explicit "Instruction does not dominate all uses", "Broken function found", or verifier diagnostic appears in the retrieved hunks.
Reproducer link: The added and updated tests exercise a branch/switch CFG rewrite involving an undef-producing PHI and a conditional loop exit.; This is not the compact C reproducer or an explicit -O1 verifier-crash regression from the issue.
Pass or subsystem link: SimplifyCFG; Transforms/Utils; scalar CFG rewriting
Causal explanation: This is a plausible verifier-sensitive candidate because SimplifyCFG rewrites branches, creates an early switch block, and changes value use placement in CFGs. However, the shown fix addresses poison/undef speculation and control-flow semantics, not dominance preservation; the inserted freeze is immediately used by the rewritten branch. The retrieved evidence therefore supplies subsystem proximity but no direct evidence of the reported non-dominating use.
Causal confidence: 0.30
Build risk: Implementation and focused SimplifyCFG transform tests are changed together.; Regression coverage includes both MemorySanitizer and non-MemorySanitizer variants of the undef/poison case.; No verifier-specific regression test or reported C reproducer is added in the retrieved hunks.

+    // There can be an unintended UB if extra values are Poison. Before the
+    // transformation, extra values may not be evaluated according to the
+    // condition, and it will not raise UB. But after transformation, we are
+    // evaluating extra values before checking the condition, and it will raise
+    // UB. It can be solved by adding freeze instruction to extra values.
+    AssumptionCache *AC = Options.AC;
+
+    if (!isGuaranteedNotToBeUndefOrPoison(ExtraCase, AC, BI, nullptr))
+      ExtraCase = Builder.CreateFreeze(ExtraCase);

define void @test_msan() sanitize_memory {
; CHECK-LABEL: @test_msan(
; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[WHILE_BODY:%.*]]
; CHECK:       while.body:
; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[WHILE_BODY_I:%.*]]
; CHECK:       while.body.i:
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[MAYBE_UNDEF:%.*]] = phi i1 [ undef, [[WHILE_BODY]] ], [ [[NEXT_MAYBE_UNDEF:%.*]], [[WHILE_BODY_I]] ]
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[C:%.*]] = call fastcc signext i8 @next_char()
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[C_10:%.*]] = icmp eq i8 [[C]], 10
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[C_13:%.*]] = icmp eq i8 [[C]], 13
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[C_10_OR_13:%.*]] = or i1 [[C_10]], [[C_13]]
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[NEXT_MAYBE_UNDEF]] = or i1 [[MAYBE_UNDEF]], [[C_10_OR_13]]
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[C_NOT_10_OR_13:%.*]] = xor i1 [[C_10_OR_13]], true
; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[C_NOT_10_OR_13]], label [[WHILE_BODY_I]], label [[WHILE_BODY_I_BREAK:%.*]]
; CHECK:       while.body.i.break:
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP0:%.*]] = freeze i1 [[MAYBE_UNDEF]]
; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[TMP0]], label [[WHILE_BODY]], label [[SWITCH_EARLY_TEST:%.*]]
; CHECK:       switch.early.test:
; CHECK-NEXT:    switch i8 [[C]], label [[RETURN:%.*]] [
; CHECK-NEXT:    i8 13, label [[WHILE_BODY]]
; CHECK-NEXT:    i8 10, label [[WHILE_BODY]]
; CHECK-NEXT:    ]
; CHECK:       return:
; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
;

entry:
  br label %while.body

while.body:
  br label %while.body.i

while.body.i:
  %maybe_undef = phi i1 [ undef, %while.body ], [ %next_maybe_undef, %while.body.i ]
  %c = call fastcc signext i8 @next_char()
  %c_10 = icmp eq i8 %c, 10
  %c_13 = icmp eq i8 %c, 13
  %c_10_or_13 = or i1 %c_10, %c_13
  %next_maybe_undef = or i1 %maybe_undef, %c_10_or_13
  %c_not_10_or_13 = xor i1 %c_10_or_13, true
  br i1 %c_not_10_or_13, label %while.body.i, label %while.body.i.break

while.body.i.break:
  ; NEXT_MAYBE_UNDEF is never undef if here
  br i1 %next_maybe_undef, label %while.body, label %return


return:
  ret void
}

top_candidates.subject: Revert "[SLP]Workaround for InsertSubVector cost."
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit reverts an SLP InsertSubVector-cost workaround, as reflected by revised AArch64 SLPVectorizer output expectations. The expected no-accelerate output again scalarizes the first lanes and vectorizes later lanes through two-lane math intrinsics and shuffle-based insertion, rather than retaining scalar calls and insertelement operations through the final lane.
Changed symbols: int_sin_4x; exp_4x; log_4x; sin_4x; cos_4x; SLPVectorizer
Behavioral change: Changes expected SLP vectorization output for AArch64 no-accelerate configurations.; Restores formation of two-lane vector calls such as llvm.exp.v2f32, llvm.log.v2f32, llvm.sin.v2f32, and llvm.cos.v2f32 for later lanes.; Restores poison-based insertelement and shufflevector assembly of the final four-lane result in the affected expectations.; Updates expectations for scalar lane-one sin handling in the int_sin_4x tests.
Assertion or trace link: No verifier assertion, dominance diagnostic, backend fatal error, or "Instruction does not dominate all uses" text is present in the retrieved hunks.
Reproducer link: The retrieved tests are AArch64 vector-math and insert/shuffle code-generation expectations, not the compact C -O1 crash reproducer.; Although poison values occur in the expected IR, no invalid use or verifier failure is demonstrated.
Pass or subsystem link: SLPVectorizer; AArch64 vector-function lowering expectations
Causal explanation: The commit concerns SLP cost/output selection and its retrieved evidence is limited to test expectation changes. It does not show a source change that manipulates CFGs, PHIs, replacement utilities, or dominance information. Poison-bearing vector IR makes this broadly optimizer-relevant, but there is no evidence-backed connection to the reported domination verifier failure.
Causal confidence: 0.06
Build risk: Retrieved evidence consists only of SLPVectorizer test updates; no implementation hunk is among the retrieved hunks.; The selected output coverage is target-specific AArch64 and uses both undef- and poison-insertelement test variants.; Many commit hunks are omitted from retrieval, so source-level build impact cannot be established from the available evidence.

top_candidates.subject: [LoopUtils] Fix incorrect RT check bounds of loop-invariant mem accesses
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This corrects runtime alias-check bounds for loop-invariant memory accesses. RuntimePointerChecking::insert now extends ScEnd by the accessed element's store size before recording the pointer range, ensuring that the stored end bound describes the full accessed object; the associated LoopVectorize tests are updated for the resulting runtime-check and vector-loop CFG expression changes.
Changed symbols: RuntimePointerChecking::insert; RuntimeCheckingPtrGroup; expandBounds; LoopVectorize
Behavioral change: Computes the pointer index type from the module DataLayout and obtains the accessed element store size through ScalarEvolution.; Adds the element-size SCEV to ScEnd before Pointers.emplace_back records the pointer range.; Removes the formerly located end-bound adjustment from its previous location in RuntimePointerChecking::insert.; Changes expected loop-vectorization runtime-check and vector-epilogue expression numbering in invariant-load and invariant-store tests.
Assertion or trace link: No explicit verifier failure, "Instruction does not dominate all uses", "Broken function found", or backend fatal-error output appears in the retrieved code or tests.
Reproducer link: The tests cover conditional invariant loads and stores that require LoopVectorize runtime pointer checks.; They do not provide the issue's compact C testcase or demonstrate a verifier abort at -O1.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopAccessAnalysis; RuntimePointerChecking; LoopUtils; LoopVectorize
Causal explanation: The change can alter whether and how LoopVectorize emits runtime alias checks and associated vector/epilogue CFGs, so it is optimizer and CFG adjacent. But its direct purpose is correcting memory-range bounds, and the retrieved implementation does not move instruction uses, repair PHIs, or maintain dominance state. Consequently, the evidence supports only a weak indirect connection to a domination-verifier failure.
Causal confidence: 0.16
Build risk: Implementation changes span LoopAccessAnalysis and LoopUtils, with X86 LoopVectorize regression expectations updated.; The change relies on existing DataLayout and ScalarEvolution APIs to construct the additional bound expression.; No verifier-focused test or direct crash reproducer is present in the retrieved hunks.

top_candidates.subject: [CostModel][X86] Adjust sext/zext SSE/AVX legalized costs based on llvm-mca reports.
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The retrieved change is test-only and revises X86 SLPVectorizer expectations after adjusted legalized sext/zext costs. In the affected two-element i8-to-i64 cases, SSE2 is now expected to retain scalar loads/extensions and assemble the result with insertelement, whereas SLM and AVX remain expected to use vector loads and vector extensions; related four-element i16-to-i64 checks are consolidated to an SSE expectation.
Changed symbols: loadext_2i8_to_2i64; loadext_4i16_to_4i64
Behavioral change: SLPVectorizer test expectations change for X86 legalization-cost decisions for sext and zext.; For SSE2 i8-to-i64 extension cases, expected output changes from a vector load/vector extension to two scalar loads, scalar extensions, and insertelement reconstruction.; The poison variants use poison as the initial insertelement vector, while the non-poison variants use undef.; No cost-model implementation or SLPVectorizer source change is present in the retrieved hunks.
Reproducer link: The affected tests are direct -slp-vectorizer tests and do not contain the reported compact C testcase, an -O1 invocation, verifier output, or a backend fatal error.
Pass or subsystem link: SLPVectorizer; X86 cost model
Causal explanation: The candidate changes expected vectorization profitability, not a visible dominance-preservation mechanism. Although the resulting expected IR includes value assembly through insertelement, all shown values are produced in a straight-line function entry block, with no CFG or cross-block use that would evidence the reported domination failure. With only test updates retrieved, there is no direct causal evidence that this commit can create invalid IR or trigger the verifier failure in PR50585.
Causal confidence: 0.03
Build risk: Retrieved changes are regression-test expectation updates only.; Coverage includes both undef- and poison-based insertelement test variants.; No implementation, verifier, CFG utility, or build configuration hunk was retrieved.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: The retrieved first-parent hunks update X86 SLPVectorizer test expectations for narrow integer-to-floating-point casts. They remove several SSE/SLM/AVX-specific expected output blocks for sitofp/uitofp alternate-cast tests, simplify FileCheck prefix usage, and change expectations for two-element i16/i8-to-double conversions so SSE is expected to form vector loads/conversions while AVX retains scalar operations in the shown cases. The retrieved evidence contains no implementation hunk.

The retrieved evidence contains no implementation hunk.
Changed symbols: sitofp_uitofp_4i32_8i16_16i8; sitofp_2i16_2f64; sitofp_2i8_2f64
Behavioral change: The SLPVectorizer's expected X86 cost-driven vectorization choices change for i8/i16 sitofp and uitofp patterns.; For the shown sitofp-to-double tests, SSE is expected to use a packed load, packed conversion, and packed store, whereas the AVX expectation remains scalar loads, scalar conversions, and scalar stores.; Target-specific alternate-cast output checks are removed in favor of the common CHECK expectations shown in the function context.

Pass or subsystem link: SLPVectorizer X86 tests; X86 cost-model behavior for narrow integer-to-floating-point conversions
Causal explanation: This is optimizer-related and can alter whether SLP vectorization is selected, but the visible changes concern expected code generation for casts and vector packing rather than CFG restructuring, dominance maintenance, or value replacement. With no implementation hunk or verifier failure in the retrieved evidence, there is no direct causal link to PR50585's invalid-IR domination failure.

top_candidates.subject: [CostModel][X86] Adjust sext/zext SSE/AVX legalized costs based on llvm-mca reports.
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The retrieved first-parent hunks revise X86 SLPVectorizer tests for sign- and zero-extension profitability. In the shown SSE2 cases, expected output changes from vector loads plus vector sext/zext to scalar loads, scalar extensions, and insertelement reconstruction; other shown configurations retain packed extension expectations. The changes also adjust expected vector-width handling for i16-to-i64 extension tests. The retrieved diff is test-only.
Changed symbols: loadext_2i8_to_2i64; loadext_4i16_to_4i64
Behavioral change: For the shown SSE2 i8-to-i64 extension cases, the expected SLP result changes from a packed load and vector sext/zext to two scalar loads/extensions followed by insertelement operations.; The poison variants expect the same scalar reconstruction but use poison as the initial insertelement vector.; The expected handling of the shown i16-to-i64 extension case changes from separate SSE2 and SLM output shapes to a shared SSE packed-extension expectation.
Assertion or trace link: No verifier assertion, dominance diagnostic, broken-function message, or backend fatal-error output is present in the retrieved hunks.
Reproducer link: The visible coverage consists of opt/SLPVectorizer IR tests for extension patterns, not the reported clang -O1 compact-C reproducer.
Pass or subsystem link: SLPVectorizer X86 tests; X86 legalized sext/zext cost-model behavior
Causal explanation: The change is plausibly relevant to optimizer selection because it changes when SLP vectorization is expected to be profitable. However, the visible transformations are straight-line load/extend/insertelement sequences and do not show control-flow edits, PHI rewrites, or cross-block use replacement that would directly explain a dominance violation. The retrieved evidence therefore supports only a weak, indirect connection.
Causal confidence: 0.07
Build risk: The retrieved diff contains only test expectation changes, with no visible implementation source edit.; Coverage reports no omitted hunks, making the available evidence complete for the retrieved diff but still limited to tests.; The tests distinguish SSE2, SLM, and AVX behavior and include poison-sensitive variants, so expectation failures may be target-specific.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The retrieved change is test-only and updates AArch64 SLPVectorizer expectations after a cost-model change for i8 vector loads and stores. The loadi8 test now expects four scalar byte computations to be vectorized into a <4 x i8> load, widened vector arithmetic and comparisons, truncation, and a <4 x i8> store. The gather-root test similarly changes MAX-COST expectations from two <2 x i8> operations plus shuffle assembly to one <4 x i8> operation.
Changed symbols: f_noalias; PR32038; SLPVectorizer AArch64 loadi8 test; SLPVectorizer AArch64 gather-root test; FileCheck CHECK/MAX-COST expectations
Behavioral change: No AArch64 cost-model or SLPVectorizer implementation hunk is included; the retrieved changes are FileCheck expectations only.; f_noalias is expected to use one contiguous <4 x i8> load and store with vector zext, multiply, add, comparisons, select, and truncation rather than four scalar byte computations.; PR32038 MAX-COST expectations change from paired <2 x i8> loads/comparisons and shuffle reconstruction to a single <4 x i8> load/comparison and direct vector select.
Pass or subsystem link: SLPVectorizer; AArch64 target cost model; LLVM transform test suite
Causal explanation: This commit is optimizer-adjacent because it changes expected SLP vectorization profitability for AArch64 byte loads/stores. The resulting expected IR includes vector construction and replacement of scalar instruction groups, but the retrieved diff does not alter the code that performs those rewrites. Summary: The retrieved change is test-only and revises X86 SLPVectorizer expected IR for SSE-legalized fp/int conversion costs. In particular, the alternate-cast tests now expect SSE to form small vector casts and shuffles instead of scalar extract/cast/insertelement sequences, and other tests remove long scalar conversion expectations. The subject identifies a cost-model adjustment, but no implementation hunk for that adjustment is available here.
Changed symbols: SLPVectorizer X86 test RUN directives; sitofp_uitofp_4i32_8i16_16i8; uitofp_16i16_16f32; sitofp_16i16_16f32; FileCheck SSE/SLM/AVX/AVX512 prefixes
Behavioral change: No production pass, cost-model, verifier, or IR-rewriting code is shown as changed.; The alternate-cast test expectations change from scalar extraction and insertion of i16/i8 casts to vector shuffles, vector sitofp/uitofp operations, and vector assembly of the final result for SSE.; The test expectations for 16-element i16-to-float conversions remove explicit scalar load/cast/store sequences, consistent with altered SLP profitability decisions.; RUN lines are mechanically converted to FileCheck --check-prefixes syntax.
Pass or subsystem link: SLPVectorizer; X86 target cost model; InstCombine in test pipelines; LLVM transform test suite
Causal explanation: The expected output exercises vector cast/shuffle construction, so an underlying SLP cost-model change could affect optimizer choices. Nevertheless, all retrieved hunks are tests and do not demonstrate a change to the transformation machinery that places instructions, replaces values, or preserves dominance. There is also no verifier failure, dominance diagnostic, CFG-sensitive test, or PR50585 reproducer evidence. The causal connection to the reported invalid-IR verifier abort is consequently weak.
Causal confidence: 0.05

The test expectations for 16-element i16-to-float conversions remove explicit scalar load/cast/store sequences, consistent with altered SLP profitability decisions.
RUN lines are mechanically converted to FileCheck --check-prefixes syntax.

issue_link.explanation: The expected output exercises vector cast/shuffle construction, so an underlying SLP cost-model change could affect optimizer choices. Nevertheless, all retrieved hunks are tests and do not demonstrate a change to the transformation machinery that places instructions, replaces values, or preserves dominance. There is also no verifier failure, dominance diagnostic, CFG-sensitive test, or PR50585 reproducer evidence. The causal connection to the reported invalid-IR verifier abort is consequently weak.

top_candidates.subject: [SLP][COST][X86]Improve cost model for masked gather.
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The retrieved change updates SLPVectorizer and LoopVectorize test expectations for the X86 masked-gather cost-model work. In particular, the SLP gather-load tests now expect an AVX vector pack/add/store sequence rather than a series of scalar loads, adds, and stores; other changes adjust expected loop-vectorization structure, FileCheck temporary names, and AVX512 feature-specific check prefixes. No implementation hunk for the cost model itself is available in the retrieved evidence.
Changed symbols: test_gather_not_profitable_pr48429; gather_load_2; lookahead_limit_users_budget; SLPVectorizer; LoopVectorize
Behavioral change: The tests now expect AVX SLP vectorization of four gathered scalar loads into insertelement operations, a vector add, and a vector store in gather_load_2.; The LoopVectorize expected output for test_gather_not_profitable_pr48429 no longer includes the previously checked unrolled vector preheader and associated induction PHIs.; AVX512 FileCheck expectations are split into AVX512F and AVX512VL-specific prefixes.
Assertion or trace link: No retrieved hunk contains "Instruction does not dominate all uses", "Broken function found", verifier output, or a fatal-error diagnostic.
Reproducer link: The changed tests exercise X86 gather/vectorization profitability and output shape, not the compact C -O1 reproducer described for PR50585.
Pass or subsystem link: SLPVectorizer cost modeling; LoopVectorize X86 gather/scatter test coverage
Causal explanation: A cost-model change can alter whether SLP vectorization is selected and therefore expose different IR-rewrite paths, but the retrieved evidence is test-only and shows no dominance, CFG, RAUW, or instruction-placement implementation change. The available hunks do not directly connect this candidate to the verifier domination failure.
Causal confidence: 0.12
Build risk: All retrieved hunks are test expectation updates; no implementation compilation risk is demonstrated by the available evidence.; FileCheck numbering and vectorization-output expectations changed, so X86 vectorizer regression tests are the primary testability signal.; The AVX512 check-prefix split can reveal target-feature-specific expectation mismatches.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This revert restores the prior behavior of removing volatile stores that precede an `unreachable` terminator. It removes guards in `SimplifyCFGOpt::simplifyUnreachable` and `markAliveBlocks` that had preserved volatile stores, and updates InstCombine/SimplifyCFG expectations so such paths simplify to `llvm.trap`/`unreachable` or an `llvm.assume`-based form rather than retaining the volatile store and associated CFG.
Changed symbols: SimplifyCFGOpt::simplifyUnreachable; markAliveBlocks; UnreachableInst; StoreInst::isVolatile; llvm.trap; llvm.assume
Behavioral change: SimplifyCFG may now delete a volatile `StoreInst` when scanning instructions before an `unreachable` terminator, rather than stopping at that store.; Local dead-block/liveness processing may now process blocks containing volatile stores instead of explicitly skipping those stores.; Affected test expectations show unreachable paths being collapsed to `llvm.trap` followed by `unreachable`, and one conditional case being reduced to an `llvm.assume`.
Assertion or trace link: No retrieved hunk mentions 'Instruction does not dominate all uses', 'Broken function found', verifier failure, or a backend fatal error.
Reproducer link: The visible regression coverage concerns volatile stores before unreachable code, trapping loads, and CFG simplification; it does not match the stated compact C testcase or specifically demonstrate an -O1 verifier abort.
Pass or subsystem link: SimplifyCFG; Transforms/Utils Local dead-code/liveness handling; InstCombine regression coverage
Causal explanation: The commit changes a CFG/dead-instruction simplification path, which can in principle affect reachability and the validity of values used across rewritten blocks. However, the shown edits only relax preservation of volatile stores on already-unreachable paths; they do not show value replacement, PHI repair, or dominance-update logic. The evidence therefore establishes broad CFG-transform risk but not a concrete path to the reported non-dominating instruction use.

The new tests exercise fallback decisions around unknown, pure, and omp_no_openmp calls; state-machine handling across direct, interprocedural, recursive, and weak calls; target init/deinit insertion; and single-threaded-execution remarks.
Changed symbols: openmp-opt; custom_state_machines; custom_state_machines_remarks; unknown_pure; __kmpc_target_init; __kmpc_target_deinit; kernel; remove_globalization
Behavioral change: Adds expected openmp-opt behavior for selecting customized generic-mode state machines and falling back when calls may contain unknown OpenMP parallel regions.; Updates OpenMP globalization expectations so target kernels include __kmpc_target_init and __kmpc_target_deinit calls and associated attributes.; Adds diagnostic/remark checks for state-machine fallback and for basic blocks classified as single-threaded.

In particular, optimized pipelines retain the call to `fn1` in `fn2b` instead of substituting its argument-derived value, and returned-argument propagation is checked so that `incdec` returns its pointer argument and the caller stores through the returned call result. Summary: This Attributor fix updates tests to preserve calls or returned arguments where replacing a value would be unsafe. In particular, optimized pipelines retain the call to `fn1` in `fn2b` instead of substituting its argument-derived value, and returned-argument propagation is checked so that `incdec` returns its pointer argument and the caller stores through the returned call result. The commit subject explicitly identifies the prevented condition as replacement with a non-dominating instruction.
Changed symbols: Attributor; fn2b; fn1; fn0; incdec; caller; return-argument.ll; PR26044.ll
Behavioral change: For `fn2b`, the old and CGSCC optimized expectations now preserve `call i64 @fn1(i64 %div)` and return its result, while the new-pass-manager expectation continues to return `%div` directly.; Returned-value propagation is expected to mark arguments as `returned` and replace `ret ... undef` with returns of the corresponding formal argument in affected optimized configurations.; In `caller`, the expected store destination changes from the original alloca `%q` to `%w`, the value returned by `incdec`, preserving the specific value selected by the call result.
Assertion or trace link: Do not replace a value with a non-dominating instruction; non-dominating instruction; Instruction does not dominate all uses; Verifier
Reproducer link: The `fn2b` expectations distinguish optimized configurations that must retain a call from configurations that may directly use `%div`, showing that replacement legality is configuration- and analysis-dependent.; The returned-argument tests exercise propagation of a value across branches and from a call result into a later store, a setting where using a value unavailable on every path would violate dominance.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM Attributor; Interprocedural constant propagation; IR value replacement
Causal explanation: The commit subject directly names the exact invalid-IR mechanism implicated by PR50585: replacing a value with an instruction that does not dominate its use. The retrieved test changes corroborate that the fix prevents selected replacements by retaining calls in affected pipelines. This makes the commit highly relevant as a corrective candidate for the verifier failure, rather than evidence that it introduced the crash.
Causal confidence: 0.96
Build risk: All retrieved hunks are tests, so the exact implementation guard and its scope are not directly visible.; The tests distinguish old/new pass-manager and CGSCC outputs, indicating behavior may differ by pipeline configuration.; No build-system or public API changes are visible.

Summary: This commit is explicitly titled "Do not replace a value with a non-dominating instruction" and updates Attributor/IPConstantProp regression checks accordingly. In particular, the expected output now distinguishes configurations where calls such as @fn1 in @fn2b remain rather than being replaced, and it checks returned-argument propagation for @incdec and its caller. The visible tests therefore support a change to Attributor value replacement whose required safety condition is instruction dominance, although the implementation hunk enforcing that condition is not included in the retrieved material.
Changed symbols: Attributor; IPConstantProp; fn0; fn1; fn2b; incdec; caller; return-argument
Behavioral change: Adds or enforces a dominance precondition before replacing a value with an instruction, as stated by the commit subject.; Updates @fn2b expectations so some Attributor configurations retain the @fn1 call and return its result instead of universally replacing it with the pre-call division result.; Updates returned-argument checks for @incdec so the old-pass-manager checked form returns its pointer argument and the caller stores through the returned call result.; Separates expected output across Attributor execution configurations, showing that the replacement behavior is not assumed to be identical for all pass-manager paths.

Pass or subsystem link: LLVM Attributor; IPConstantProp; Attributor value replacement and returned-argument inference
Causal explanation: This is a strong causal match: replacing a use with an instruction that does not dominate that use is precisely the condition that produces LLVM's "Instruction does not dominate all uses" verifier failure. The commit subject states that it prevents this exact class of replacement. While the visible tests do not explicitly name pr50585 and the implementation hunk is unavailable, the invariant and failure mode align directly.

The retrieved hunks update Attributor tests for recursive functions, norecurse inference, nonnull-related recursion, and argument-promotion behavior, differentiating results by CGSCC and pass-manager pipeline. The visible changes demonstrate altered expected call elimination and inferred attributes, but no implementation hunk is available to independently establish the precise traversal algorithm.

steps.subject: [DivRemPairs] Add an initial case for hoisting to a common predecessor.

evidence: DivRemPairs now physically hoists existing udiv/urem instructions from branch blocks into a common predecessor, directly requiring operand and use dominance preservation.

The shown logic checks control-flow transfer safety but does not visibly establish that every operand of a moved division/remainder dominates the predecessor insertion point; block-local operands can produce exactly the reported verifier failure.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes `optimizeDivRem` in the Scalar `DivRemPairs` pass to hoist a division, and optionally its paired remainder, from a triangle-shaped pair of blocks into their common predecessor. It recognizes a remainder block with one successor leading to the division block, requires the predecessor to branch only to those two blocks, and checks that instructions preceding each operation are guaranteed to transfer execution. The associated tests expect the hoisted operations to dominate both paths and, for the i128 case, expect a remainder to be decomposed into `mul`/`sub` using frozen operands.
Changed symbols: optimizeDivRem; DivRemPairsPass; DivRemPairsLegacyPass; IsSafeToHoist; remainder_triangle_i64; remainder_triangle_i128; remainder_triangle_i64_multiple_rem_edges
Behavioral change: Adds cross-basic-block hoisting of `udiv` from the division block to a common predecessor when the predecessor reaches only the division or remainder blocks.; When a target div/rem operation is available, also hoists the paired remainder; otherwise it leaves the remainder in place so later logic can rewrite it as multiplication/subtraction.; Uses `isGuaranteedToTransferExecutionToSuccessor` to prevent hoisting across instructions that may stop execution, such as potentially throwing operations.; Causes the hoisted division to dominate the branch into both the remainder and division paths in the newly covered triangle cases.
Assertion or trace link: Instruction does not dominate all uses; Verifier; dominance
Reproducer link: The new regression shape places `urem` and `udiv` on converging control-flow paths, which is a CFG/value-placement pattern relevant to verifier dominance failures.
Pass or subsystem link: llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/DivRemPairs.cpp; Scalar optimizer instruction motion
Causal explanation: This is a direct scalar-optimizer instruction-motion change in a pass that receives a `DominatorTree`. The new guard proves control-flow reachability and non-throwing prefixes, but the visible hunk does not prove that every operand of a moved `DivInst` or `RemInst` dominates the insertion point in `PredBB`. If an operand is defined in the original Div/Rem block before the moved operation, moving the user before that definition can create exactly the verifier condition that an instruction does not dominate one of its uses. The retrieved tests use function arguments, so they do not exercise such block-local operand definitions; there is no direct evidence that the issue reproducer reaches this pass at `-O1`.
Causal confidence: 0.76
Build risk: Modifies production Scalar optimizer code that moves existing IR instructions between basic blocks.; The pass preserves CFG analyses because it does not alter edges, but the change is sensitive to SSA operand dominance and instruction ordering.; Regression coverage adds triangle CFG cases and a may-throw negative case, but the visible tests do not cover operands defined before the moved division or remainder in their original blocks.; No dedicated verifier regression test is included in the retrieved hunks.

top_candidates.subject: [IndVars] Don't widen pointers in WidenIV::getWideRecurrence
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The IndVarSimplify change narrows WidenIV::getWideRecurrence eligibility from all ScalarEvolution-supported types to integer types only, explicitly preventing pointer induction-variable uses from being widened. The accompanying signed-trip-count test changes its data layout to include 32-bit pointers, consistent with exercising pointer-type handling.
Changed symbols: WidenIV::getWideRecurrence; llvm/lib/Transforms/Utils/SimplifyIndVar.cpp; llvm/test/Transforms/IndVarSimplify/signed-trip-count.ll
Behavioral change: WidenIV::getWideRecurrence no longer widens a narrow use merely because ScalarEvolution considers its type SCEVable.; Pointer-typed narrow uses are rejected because the new guard requires an integer type.; The regression test data layout now explicitly defines 32-bit pointers, increasing coverage of pointer-related induction-variable behavior.
Reproducer link: The issue is an optimizer-produced invalid-IR failure at -O1; this change modifies an optimizer rewrite that can replace or widen induction-variable values.
Pass or subsystem link: IndVarSimplify; Transforms/Utils; ScalarEvolution
Causal explanation: This is a plausible link because the change disables a previously permitted pointer widening path in an induction-variable transformation. Such rewrites can affect the placement and replacement of SSA values, which is relevant to a verifier report that an instruction does not dominate all uses. However, the retrieved hunk contains no verifier diagnostic, dominance-specific logic, or reproducer matching pr50585, so the connection is indirect rather than demonstrated.
Causal confidence: 0.45

top_candidates.subject: [RS4GC] Use one DVCache for both inlineGetBaseAndOffset() and insertParsePoints()
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: RewriteStatepointsForGC now creates one DefiningValueMapTy cache in RewriteStatepointsForGC::runOnFunction and passes it to both inlineGetBaseAndOffset and insertParsePoints, instead of using separate cache lifetimes. The stated purpose is to avoid duplicate base PHIs and selects, and the statepoint test is updated to expect reuse of one selected base value.
Changed symbols: RewriteStatepointsForGC::runOnFunction; inlineGetBaseAndOffset; insertParsePoints; DefiningValueMapTy; findBasePointers; test_duplicate_base_generation
Behavioral change: A single defining-value cache is shared across get-base-and-offset inlining and parse-point insertion.; Base-PHI/select discovery can reuse values created or discovered by the earlier phase rather than independently generating duplicates.; The statepoint regression test now expects one selected base value in the gc-live bundle instead of a duplicate selected base.
Reproducer link: The retrieved test covers duplicate base generation for GC statepoints, not the compact C -O1 reproducer described for pr50585.
Pass or subsystem link: RewriteStatepointsForGC; Transforms/Scalar; DominatorTree; GC statepoints
Causal explanation: The change operates in a dominance-aware transformation: insertParsePoints receives a DominatorTree and rewrites base PHIs/selects, so incorrect reuse of cached defining values could in principle affect SSA availability. The available evidence instead presents the cache sharing as a duplicate-elimination improvement, and pr50585 provides no GC-statepoint or statepoint-strategy indication. Therefore the subsystem-level relationship to dominance is real but the specific issue link is weak.
Causal confidence: 0.16
Build risk: Function signatures for inlineGetBaseAndOffset and insertParsePoints change to require a shared cache argument.; The cache lifetime expands to cover both transformation phases within runOnFunction.; A targeted RewriteStatepointsForGC output test is updated to check deduplicated base generation.

Summary: This commit replaces hand-maintained verifier rules for whether attributes apply to functions, returns, and parameters with TableGen-derived Attribute::canUseAsFnAttr, canUseAsRetAttr, and canUseAsParamAttr queries. It restructures Verifier::verifyAttributeTypes to retain type/category checking while moving location-applicability checks into the parameter-, function-, and return-attribute verification paths, and updates intrinsic-call attribute validation to use the new property queries.
Changed symbols: Verifier::verifyAttributeTypes; Verifier::verifyParameterAttrs; Verifier::verifyFunctionAttrs; Verifier::visitIntrinsicCall; isFuncOnlyAttr; isFuncOrArgAttr; Attribute::canUseAsParamAttr; Attribute::canUseAsFnAttr
Behavioral change: Function, return, and parameter attribute applicability is checked per attribute through TableGen-derived canUseAs*Attr predicates.; The manually maintained isFuncOnlyAttr and isFuncOrArgAttr classification helpers are removed.; Intrinsic-call validation distinguishes parameter-usable and function-usable attributes through the new Attribute property APIs.; Verifier::verifyAttributeTypes no longer receives an IsFunction flag; placement-specific validation is performed by its callers.
Assertion or trace link: Verifier; Broken function
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM IR Verifier; LLVM IR attribute validation
Causal explanation: This is directly in the verifier subsystem that emits verifier failures and backend fatal-error output after malformed IR is detected. A wrong TableGen property could change whether malformed attribute placement is diagnosed or accepted. Nevertheless, the retrieved hunks only alter attribute applicability checks; they contain no scalar optimization, CFG rewrite, SSA replacement, or dominance-maintenance logic. They therefore could change verifier reporting for attribute-invalid IR, but provide no direct mechanism for producing the reported non-dominating instruction use.

Summary: This is an NFC test-only change that adds DivRemPairs IR cases for triangular control-flow shapes, including simple conditional and multi-edge switch variants where a urem occurs on one path and a udiv occurs in a joining block. The added CHECK expectations document the pre-existing placement of the division and remainder rather than modifying optimizer implementation code.
Changed symbols: remainder_triangle_i64; remainder_triangle_i128; remainder_triangle_i64_multiple_rem_edges; remainder_triangle_i64_multiple_div_edges; DivRemPairs X86 div-expanded-rem-pair.ll CHECKs
Behavioral change: Adds regression coverage for CFG shapes relevant to making a division dominate a remainder.; Does not change production pass, CFG, value-replacement, or verifier behavior in the retrieved hunk.
Assertion or trace link: No verifier assertion, "Instruction does not dominate all uses", "Broken function found", or fatal-error diagnostic is referenced in the retrieved hunk.
Reproducer link: The tests construct branch and switch CFGs with urem and udiv in different blocks, a shape relevant to dominance-sensitive DivRemPairs transformations.; No compact C reproducer, -O1 invocation, crash, or abort is added.
Pass or subsystem link: DivRemPairs test coverage; LLVM scalar-transform test infrastructure

+;;   {

+;;       }
+;;     }

+;;   }

+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[DOTTHREADID_TEMP_:%.*]] = alloca i32, align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 0, i32* [[DOTZERO_ADDR]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP0:%.*]] = call i32 @__kmpc_target_init(%struct.ident_t* @[[GLOB1]], i1 true, i1 false, i1 true)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXEC_USER_CODE:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[TMP0]], -1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXEC_USER_CODE]], label [[USER_CODE_ENTRY:%.*]], label [[WORKER_EXIT:%.*]]

+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP1:%.*]] = call i32 @__kmpc_global_thread_num(%struct.ident_t* @[[GLOB1]]) #[[ATTR2:[0-9]+]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[TMP1]], i32* [[DOTTHREADID_TEMP_]], align 4

top_candidates.subject: [DivRemPairs] Add an initial case for hoisting to a common predecessor.
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Extends the DivRemPairs scalar pass to hoist matching division/remainder operations from a triangle-shaped CFG into a common predecessor. When the remainder block has a unique predecessor, flows only to the division block, and instructions before both operations are guaranteed to transfer execution, optimizeDivRem moves the division, and optionally the remainder, before the predecessor terminator. The tests are updated to expect the hoisted operations and, for i128, subsequent remainder decomposition into multiply/subtract using the hoisted division.
Changed symbols: optimizeDivRem; DivRemPairsPass::run; DivRemPairsLegacyPass; remainder_triangle_i64; remainder_triangle_i128; remainder_triangle_i64_multiple_rem_edges
Behavioral change: Adds a new CFG rewrite that moves DivInst and, for direct div/rem pairs, RemInst from successor blocks into PredBB.; Marks the division as dominating after hoisting so the pass can reuse it for remainder pairing or expand a remainder into mul/sub.; Restricts the transformation using predecessor/successor shape checks and isGuaranteedToTransferExecutionToSuccessor checks for instructions preceding the moved operations.; Does not visibly check that every operand of the moved division or remainder is available and dominating at the new insertion point in PredBB.
Assertion or trace link: Instruction does not dominate all uses; Broken function found; Verifier; dominance
Reproducer link: The new transformation moves arithmetic instructions across basic-block boundaries in a conditional triangle CFG.; If a moved DivInst or RemInst uses a value defined in its original block or another non-dominating block, moveBefore(PredBB->getTerminator()) can create an IR use whose definition no longer dominates that use.; The included tests use function arguments, and the i128 test introduces freezes in the entry block; those operands already dominate the new predecessor placement and therefore do not exercise non-dominating local operands.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM DivRemPairs scalar optimization pass; LLVM IR dominance invariants; LLVM verifier
Causal explanation: This is a high-risk direct match for a verifier-detected dominance failure: the patch introduces instruction motion into a predecessor block and relies on CFG/execution-safety conditions, but the visible logic does not establish operand dominance at the new location. Such invalid motion can produce the issue's "Instruction does not dominate all uses" verifier diagnostic during optimization, including an -O1 pipeline if this pass is scheduled there.
Causal confidence: 0.88
Build risk: Changes a scalar optimizer pass that explicitly depends on DominatorTree analysis.; Adds regression coverage for successful hoisting, multi-edge CFGs, and an exception-safety negative case.; The visible tests do not cover hoisting when the moved div/rem operands are defined below the common predecessor, leaving verifier-sensitive operand-dominance behavior untested.

top_candidates.subject: [DivRemPairs] Add an initial case for hoisting to a common predecessor.
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Extends the DivRemPairs scalar optimization with a common-predecessor hoisting case. When a remainder block flows uniquely to a division block, all predecessor successors are those two blocks, and instructions preceding the division/remainder are guaranteed to transfer execution, the pass moves the division, and optionally the remainder, before the predecessor terminator. This enables the remainder to be decomposed into multiply/subtract when the hoisted division dominates it.
Changed symbols: optimizeDivRem; DivRemPairsLegacyPass; DivRemPairsPass::run; IsSafeToHoist; BasicBlock::getSingleSuccessor; BasicBlock::getUniquePredecessor; Instruction::moveBefore
Behavioral change: Adds a new CFG-sensitive transformation that hoists div/rem instructions from successor blocks into their common predecessor.; Sets DivDominates after hoisting the division, allowing existing div/rem pairing logic to reuse the moved division for remainder expansion.; For div/rem operation pairs, moves both operations to the predecessor; otherwise leaves the remainder in place and permits rewriting it as mul/sub.; Adds tests for triangular CFGs, i64 and i128 divisions/remainders, freeze insertion in the i128 case, and multi-edge CFG variants.
Assertion or trace link: dominance (DivDominates); common-predecessor hoisting; Instruction::moveBefore
Reproducer link: The added tests exercise a branch where urem is in one successor block and udiv is in a joining successor block, then expect the operations to be moved into the entry/common-predecessor block.; The transformation directly changes instruction placement across basic blocks, the class of rewrite that can trigger an "Instruction does not dominate all uses" verifier diagnostic if placement or operand availability is incorrect.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM Transforms/Scalar; DivRemPairs; DominatorTree; LLVM IR CFG transformation
Causal explanation: This is a direct match for the issue's high-risk area: a scalar optimizer pass performs CFG-sensitive instruction movement and explicitly changes a dominance-related state. The visible checks establish predecessor/successor shape and execution-transfer safety before moving instructions, but the new hunk itself does not show an explicit check that every operand of a moved instruction dominates PredBB. Therefore this change has a plausible mechanism for producing invalid IR with a non-dominating value or use, although the retrieved material does not establish that PR50585's compact testcase reaches DivRemPairs or this specific hoisting path.

diff --git a/lld/test/MachO/dyld-stub-binder.s b/lld/test/MachO/dyld-stub-binder.s
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..36685580b5e1
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lld/test/MachO/dyld-stub-binder.s
@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@
+# REQUIRES: aarch64
+# RUN: rm -rf %t; split-file %s %t
+# RUN: llvm-mc -filetype=obj -triple=arm64-apple-darwin %t/foo.s -o %t/foo.o
+# RUN: llvm-mc -filetype=obj -triple=arm64-apple-darwin %t/bar.s -o %t/bar.o
+# RUN: llvm-mc -filetype=obj -triple=arm64-apple-darwin %t/test.s -o %t/test.o
+
+## Dylibs that don't do lazy dynamic calls don't need dyld_stub_binder.
+# RUN: %lld -arch arm64 -dylib %t/foo.o -o %t/libfoo.dylib
+# RUN: llvm-nm -m %t/libfoo.dylib | FileCheck --check-prefix=NOSTUB %s
+
+## Dylibs that do lazy dynamic calls do need dyld_stub_binder.
+# RUN: not %lld -arch arm64 -dylib %t/bar.o %t/libfoo.dylib \
+# RUN:     -o %t/libbar.dylib 2>&1 | FileCheck --check-prefix=MISSINGSTUB %s
+# RUN: %lld -arch arm64 -lSystem -dylib %t/bar.o  %t/libfoo.dylib \
+# RUN:     -o %t/libbar.dylib
+# RUN: llvm-nm -m %t/libbar.dylib | FileCheck --check-prefix=STUB %s
+
+## As do executables.
+# RUN: not %lld -arch arm64 %t/libfoo.dylib %t/libbar.dylib %t/test.o \
+# RUN:     -o %t/test 2>&1 | FileCheck --check-prefix=MISSINGSTUB %s
+# RUN: %lld -arch arm64 -lSystem %t/libfoo.dylib %t/libbar.dylib %t/test.o \
+# RUN:     -o %t/test
+# RUN: llvm-nm -m %t/test | FileCheck --check-prefix=STUB %s
+
+## Test dynamic lookup of dyld_stub_binder.
+# RUN: %lld -arch arm64 %t/libfoo.dylib %t/libbar.dylib %t/test.o \
+# RUN:     -o %t/test -undefined dynamic_lookup
+# RUN: llvm-nm -m %t/test | FileCheck --check-prefix=DYNSTUB %s
+# RUN: %lld -arch arm64 %t/libfoo.dylib %t/libbar.dylib %t/test.o \
+# RUN:     -o %t/test -U dyld_stub_binder
+# RUN: llvm-nm -m %t/test | FileCheck --check-prefix=DYNSTUB %s
+
+# MISSINGSTUB:      error: undefined symbol: dyld_stub_binder
+# MISSINGSTUB-NEXT: >>> referenced by lazy binding (normally in libSystem.dylib)
+
+# NOSTUB-NOT: dyld_stub_binder
+# STUB: (undefined) external dyld_stub_binder (from libSystem)
+# DYNSTUB: (undefined) external dyld_stub_binder (dynamically looked up)
+
+#--- foo.s
+.globl _foo
+_foo:
+
+#--- bar.s
+.text
+.globl _bar
+_bar:
+  bl _foo
+  ret
+
+#--- test.s
+.text
+.globl _main
+
+.p2align 2
+_main:
+  bl _foo
+  bl _bar
+  ret
